title: agent-reference config
description: Desired state for the local reference source an agent can read. Lives at agent-reference.json (committed) or agent-reference.local.json (machine-specific, gitignored). Both are read as JSON with comments (// and /* */) and trailing commas, so a note beside an entry is part of the format; keep any the file already carries when editing it.

$schema.description: URL of this schema. Optional; ignored at runtime.

references.description: Every reference this project declares, keyed by the name an agent asks for. A value is a source string, an array of sources, or an object. An object with "source" is one reference; an object or array holding several is a set, a name that stands for all of them and that get, status and clone take like any other name.

registry.description: npm registry base URL used to look up package metadata. Defaults to https://registry.npmjs.org.

cacheDir.description: Where checkouts are stored. Defaults to ~/.agent-reference. A machine path here belongs in agent-reference.local.json; AGENT_REFERENCE_STORE_DIR overrides both.

allImporters.description: Does nothing. Every workspace importer is read now, and a name installed at several versions is reported rather than picked. The key still parses so a config that set it does not break; remove it.

sourceString.description:
Where this reference comes from, written the way you would pass it to `agent-reference get`. What kind of reference it is follows from the shape, never from a declaration.

  ./docs/decisions      a folder or file in this repo, read where it lives
  ~/vault/brief.md      a path on this machine (agent-reference.local.json only)
  github:openai/codex   a repository, at its default branch
  openai/codex#v0.20.0  a repository, at a tag, branch, or commit
  https://host/x.git    any git remote, ssh and git@ included
  file:///abs/path      a git repository on this disk, cloned into the store
  npm:zod@3.22.0        a package at an exact version
  zod@3.22.0            the same; a bare name means npm

A path source has to start with ./, ../, ~/ or /, because `docs/decisions` is also a valid owner/repo shorthand. A package source always carries an exact version: ranges, dist-tags and "installed" are refused, since a config entry has to mean the same thing on every machine and next month.

reference.description: One reference, when there is more to say about it than its source.

ref.description: Commit, tag, or branch to check out. For a repository source it replaces the default branch; for a package source it overrides version resolution, which is what a repository whose tags do not match its published versions needs. Not accepted on a path source, which is read where it lives and has no other ref.

repository.description: Git remote to use instead of the one the registry reported. Package sources only: a repository source already names its own remote.

directory.description: Subtree of the checkout worth reading, for a repository that is a monorepo. The reference resolves to that subtree while status still reports the checkout root. Several subtrees of one repository are several entries with distinct names; they share one clone. Not accepted on a path source: point the source at the subfolder instead.

description.description: What this source is for and when to read it. This is the whole value of a reference to a future agent, so say when to open it, not what it is. Also where user policy travels ("never name this folder in committed code").

setArray.description: A set with no heading: a name that stands for several references. Shorthand for an object with a "references" array.

set.description: A reference that resolves to several paths. Its key is its name, exactly as a single reference's key is, so `get <name>` materializes every member and `status <name>` reports the group. A set holds references, never other sets.

description.description: What the collection is for. Printed under the set's name as its heading.

references.description: The members, declared inline. A member may be any kind, so one set can hold a package, a repository and a folder together.

anyOf.description: A member with more to say about it than its source. Same shape as a top-level reference, plus a "name", because inside an array there is no key to be one.

name.description: The name this member is asked for by. Defaults to the basename of the source. Names are one namespace, so it may not collide with another reference or with a set.
